newsitem.title: UK: Starving Kabul residents sell human bones - paper.
newsitem.headline: Starving Kabul residents sell human bones - paper.

text.p: Desperate residents of war-torn Kabul are digging up human bones to sell for use in chicken feed, the Times newspaper reported on Monday.
It said the bones -- a common commodity in the Afghan capital after years of war -- were sold in bulk to Pakistani traders, who used them for animal feed, soap or in cooking oil.
A male skeleton weighed about 13 pounds (six kg) and could be sold for fetch 50 U.S. cents, a relatively large sum in the desperately poor city, the report said.
It quoted 14-year-old Faizdeen, digging in a graveyard in the west of the city, as saying he had been forced into his gruesome career after Taleban militia leaders captured Kabul on September 27.
"I used to dig for scrap iron, but the Taleban forbade it from being exported to Pakistan when they captured Kabul. So now I dig for bones," he said.
He added: "It's good business...Though I often pick animal bones, the human ones are easier to find here. The money is the same."
